title: 10 Evidence-Based Benefits of Green Tea

Green tea: Many of these benefits may be associated with certain compounds in green tea, such as catechins and L-theanine.
PRIZE Research suggests that drinking green tea may benefit cognition, mood, and brain function, possibly due to compounds in green tea like caffeine and L-theanine.
While the evidence is mixed and inconsistent, research has linked drinking green tea with a reduced chance of developing some types of cancer, such as lung cancer or ovarian cancer.
shows a modest beneficial effect, scientists could not conclude any consistent effects of green tea on overall cancer likelihood.
A 2020 study showed that green tea was linked with lower levels of certain markers related to Alzheimer’s disease in people without current, known cognitive issues.
While the evidence is mixed, studies seem to show health benefits with three to five cups (24 to 40 ounces) consumed daily.
Drinking green tea has many benefits.
It is high in antioxidants, which may help prevent or remedy cellular damage and support your overall health.
It may even have some properties that help protect against cancer and heart disease.
Some research-based evidence suggests drinking green tea can help reduce body fat, including in the abdomen.
10 Evidence-Based Benefits of Green Tea: LEAD Green tea may help support cognition and weight management, boost energy, and offer some protection against cancer.
